blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The rapid growth of video-based social media has increased users’ exposure to harmful content, creating a need for reliable automated video safety detection. Although recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show strong video understanding capabilities, existing harmful video detection systems face two key limitations: they typically reduce safety detection to binary classification, overlooking the inherently multi-label nature of unsafe videos, and they rely on static training objectives that do not support controllable precision-recall trade-offs, though the desired operating point may vary across moderation pipelines and unsafe categories. To address these gaps, we propose Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO), a reinforcement learning framework for Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD). ATPO introduces the Adaptive Tversky Reward (ATR), which dynamically adjusts false-positive and false-negative penalties during training to enable controllable precision–recall trade-offs. Experiments on SafeWatch-Bench and XD-Violence show that ATPO substantially improves multi-label performance, increasing the Jaccard Index from 40.66 to 75.44 on SafeWatch-Bench-Real. Moreover, ATR enables reliable steering of the precision–recall operating point, supporting deployment scenarios with heterogeneous policy requirements. Code and checkpoints are provided at https://bruceyg.github.io/ATPO-project-page/ .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The rapid growth of video-based social media platforms has led to an increasing amount of harmful video content 1 1 1 This paper contains content for demonstration purposes that may be disturbing for some readers. .
Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have enabled strong performance on video understanding tasks [ 25 , 17 , 2 , 1 , 5 , 41 ] , and there is a growing amount of work using VLMs for video safety detection [ 46 , 33 , 42 , 10 , 4 ] . However, existing work on harmful video detection typically formulates the task as binary classification, distinguishing safe from unsafe content while treating all unsafe categories as a single class. Such formulations overlook the multi-class structure of unsafe content and are limited in their ability to provide the fine-grained and interpretable classification outcomes required by human content moderators [ 3 , 26 ] . In practice, video safety detection is inherently multi-label : unsafe videos often involve overlapping categories (e.g., violence and abuse) due to their rich and complex semantics.

blocks.en: Moreover, prior approaches typically optimize a static training objective and evaluate models at fixed operating settings [ 47 , 9 , 10 ] . This setup does not explicitly enable controllable precision–recall trade-offs , and is therefore misaligned with real-world deployment settings. In practice, safety detection systems are often integrated as guardrails within multi-stage moderation pipelines, where the desired precision-recall operating point depends critically on policy requirements. For example, guardrail systems designed for children must prioritize high recall to minimize harmful exposure. In contrast, general-purpose moderation systems require a more balanced trade-off between precision and recall [ 38 , 6 ] . Importantly, the optimal precision-recall trade-off may also differ across unsafe categories. Multi-label safety detection inherently involves heterogeneous risk profiles. Certain categories (e.g., misinformation) may prioritize higher precision to reduce over-censorship, while others (e.g., violent or extremist content) may prioritize higher recall to minimize the risk of harmful exposure.
blocks.zh: 此外,以往的做法通常优化固定培训目标,并在固定操作环境中评价模型[47、9、10]。 这种设置没有明确允许可控制的精度-召回权衡,因此与现实世界部署设置不符. 在实践中,安全探测系统往往作为护卫铁路纳入多阶段节制管线,所期望的精确召回操作点主要取决于政策要求。 例如,为儿童设计的护卫系统必须优先高调召回,以尽量减少有害接触。 与此相反,一般目的节制制度要求在精确和召回之间达成更平衡的权衡[38,6]。 重要的是,最佳的精确召回权衡也可能因不安全类别而异。 多标签安全检测必然涉及各种风险简介。 某些类别(如错误信息)可能优先考虑提高准确度以减少过度审查,而其他类别(如暴力或极端主义内容)可能优先考虑提高召回率,以尽量减少有害接触的风险。

blocks.en: To address these gaps, we propose Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO), a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework built upon Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) [ 30 ] . We first move beyond binary supervision by designing fine-grained multi-label safety training and rewards for GRPO, and systematically study reward formulations for multi-label optimization. Building on this, we draw inspiration from feedback loops in control theory to develop the Adaptive Tversky Reward (ATR). ATR reformulates the Tversky coefficients [ 35 ] , which govern False Positive (FP) and False Negative (FN) penalties, as feedback-driven variables that dynamically adjust during training based on observed model errors. It enables controllable and category-aware safety behavior within a unified multi-label detection model. Experiments on SafeWatch-Bench [ 4 ] and XD-Violence [ 39 ] show that ATPO substantially improves Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD) over large general-purpose VLMs while maintaining strong binary performance. Furthermore, ATPO provides reliable control over the precision–recall trade-off both globally and at the category level, offering a practical mechanism for deployment.
blocks.zh: 为了弥补这些差距,我们提议采用适应性的特维尔斯基政策优化(ATPO),即基于集团相对政策优化的强化学习框架[30]。 我们首先超越二进制监督,为GRPO设计精细的多标签安全培训和奖励,系统研究多标签优化的奖励配方. 在此基础上,我们从控制理论中的反馈循环中汲取灵感,开发出适应性的特维尔斯基奖(ATR). ATR重订了Tversky系数[35],该系数规范了 False BOY(FP)和 False NOY(FN)的处罚,作为反馈驱动的变量,在训练期间根据观察到的模型错误进行动态调整. 它能够在统一的多标签检测模型中实现可控和有类别意识的安全行为. 关于安全观察-奔驰[4]和XD-暴力[39]的实验表明,ATPO在保持强二进制性能的同时,大大改进了大型通用VLM的多标签视频安全检测(Multi-VSD). 此外,ATPO对全球和类别一级的准确性-召回权衡提供了可靠的控制,为部署提供了一个切实可行的机制。

blocks.en: Our contributions can be summarized as: 1. We formulate multi-label harmful video detection under RL-based fine-tuning and systematically study reward formulations for optimizing multi-label safety objectives. 2. We propose Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO), a feedback-driven RL framework that dynamically adjusts false-positive and false-negative penalties during training via the Adaptive Tversky Reward (ATR). Extensive experiments show that ATPO substantially improves multi-label video safety detection, increasing the Jaccard Index from 40.66 to 75.44 (Section 4.2 and 4.3 ). 3. Our experiments show that ATR enables reliable control over the precision–recall trade-off both globally and at the category level, supporting deployment scenarios with different risk sensitivities (Section 4.4 ).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Prior research on video safety detection has largely been studied through the paradigm of Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) [ 31 , 19 , 39 , 23 , 24 , 28 ] , where the objective is to determine whether a video, typically recorded by surveillance cameras, contains abnormal events. Early approaches commonly formulated VAD as a binary classification problem that distinguishes normal from anomalous activities [ 31 ] . More recently, a line of work has leveraged Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for video anomaly detection and understanding [ 42 , 46 , 47 , 45 , 10 ] . For example, Holmes-VAD [ 46 ] trains a VLM with temporal sampling to detect anomalies and generate explanations for abnormal events in long videos, while VAD-R1 [ 10 ] introduces Video Anomaly Reasoning (VAR), a structured chain-of-thought pipeline further optimized with an RL-based AVA-GRPO algorithm. Beyond binary detection, recent work has begun to study fine-grained video safety and anomaly recognition. Ex-VAD [ 9 ] extends VAD to recognize multiple abnormal event categories using vision-language supervision, but formulates the task as multi-class classification, where each video is assigned a single abnormal category. Open-Vocabulary VAD [ 40 , 13 ] uses pretrained VLMs and textual semantics to detect both seen and unseen anomaly categories. More recently, SafeWatch-Bench [ 4 ] explicitly frames video safety detection as a multi-category moderation task. Despite this progress, most prior methods either focus on binary anomaly detection or assign a single abnormal category to each video. In contrast, we study Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD), where multiple harmful categories may co-occur in the same video.
blocks.zh: 之前对视频安全探测的研究主要通过视频异常探测(VAD)[31,19,39,23,24,28]的范式来研究,其目的是确定一个视频,通常由监视摄像机录制,是否包含异常事件. 早期方法通常将VAD编为二元分类问题,将正常活动与异常活动区分开来[31]. 最近,一行工作利用Vision-Langage Models(VLMs)进行视频异常检测和了解[42、46、47、45、10]。 例如,福尔摩斯-VAD [46] 训练一个带有时间采样的VLM,以检测异常现象并生成长视频中异常事件的解释,而VAD-R1 [10]引入视频异常理性(VAR),一个结构化的思维链管道,进一步优化了基于RL的AVA-GRPO算法. 除了二进制检测之外,最近的工作已经开始研究精细的视频安全和异常识别. 前VAD [9] 扩展VAD以使用视觉语言监督识别多个异常事件类别,但将任务设定为多类分类,其中每个视频被指定一个单一异常类别. 开放词汇VAD [40, 13] 使用预先训练的VLM和文字语义来检测所见和未见的异常分类. 最近,Safe Watch-Bench [4]明确将视频安全检测作为多类节制任务。 尽管取得了这一进展,大多数前期方法要么侧重于二进制异常检测,要么为每部视频指定一个单一的异常类别. 相比之下,我们研究了多标签视频安全检测(Multi-VSD),在同一视频中,多个有害类别可能共同存在.

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning has also been explored for improving the reasoning and perception capabilities of VLMs for videos [ 5 , 41 , 15 , 10 , 14 , 16 ] . Recent works apply GRPO-style RL fine-tuning to video understanding tasks, where reward functions are designed to encourage stronger temporal reasoning, spatio-temporal perception, and instruction-following abilities. Video-R1 [ 5 ] introduces reinforcement fine-tuning for video reasoning and designs temporal rewards to improve the model’s ability to reason over video frames. VideoChat-R1 [ 41 , 15 ] further studies reinforcement fine-tuning for video dialogue and spatio-temporal perception, using task-specific rewards for video question answering and temporal understanding. Other recent works investigate reward design and data efficiency for VideoLLM RL [ 14 ] , and use RL to improve temporal sampling and temporal grounding in video LLMs [ 16 ] . For safety-related tasks, GuardReasoner-VL [ 20 ] trains VLM guardrails with reasoning SFT and GRPO, while VAD-R1 [ 10 ] applies RL to structured video anomaly reasoning. These studies show that reinforcement learning provides an effective post-training mechanism for adapting VLMs to video reasoning and safety tasks. Building on these developments, we study RL-based reward design for Multi-VSD, introducing adaptive rewards that account for partial label correctness and asymmetric FP/FN costs to enable controllable precision-recall trade-offs during training.
blocks.zh: 还探索加强学习,以提高视频VLM的推理和感知能力[5,41,15,10,14,16]. 近期的作品将GPRO风格的RL微调应用到视频理解任务中,其中的奖励功能旨在鼓励更强的时空推理,时空感知,以及指令跟随能力. Video-R1[5]引入了强化精细化的视频推理,并设计了时间奖励,以提高模型在视频帧上进行推理的能力. VideoChat-R1 [41,15] 进一步研究强化微调,用于视频对话以及时空感知,利用特定任务奖励进行视频问答和时空理解. 最近的其他作品调查VideoLLM RL的奖励设计和数据效率[14],并使用RL改进视频LLMs中的时间采样和时间定位[16]. 对于安全相关任务,GuardReasoner-VL [20] 使用推理SFT和GRPO对VLM护卫铁路进行训练,而VAD-R1 [10] 将RL应用于结构化的视频异常推理. 这些研究表明,强化学习提供了一个有效的培训后机制,使VLM适应视频推理和安全任务. 在这些发展的基础上,我们研究了基于RL的多VSD奖励设计,引入了适应性奖励,考虑到部分标签正确性和不对称的FP/FN成本,以便在培训期间实现可控制的精确召回权衡.

blocks.en: Recent work also studies video safety beyond anomaly detection. For generative models, T2VSafetyBench [ 27 ] evaluates safety risks in text-to-video generation, while SAFREE [ 44 ] provides a training-free safeguard for text-to-image and video generation. For video and multimodal LLMs, VideoSafety-R1 [ 32 ] combines alarm-token-guided SFT with safety-guided GRPO to improve defensive reasoning. SafeVid [ 36 ] constructs video-specific safety preference data and applies Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) [ 29 ] , whereas SEA [ 22 ] uses synthetic modality embeddings to enable low-resource safety alignment from textual data. Complementary security and privacy studies examine video-modality jailbreaks through VideoJail [ 8 ] and protective adversarial watermarks that disrupt unauthorized video annotation [ 18 ] . These directions address safe generation, safe-response alignment, or protection against misuse of video inputs. ATPO instead studies moderation of existing videos through fine-grained multi-label predictions.
blocks.zh: 最近的工作还研究了超越异常探测的视频安全性. 对于基因模型,T2VSafety Bench[27]评价了文本到视频生成中的安全风险,而SAFREE[44]为文本到图像和视频生成提供了无培训保障. 对于视频和多模式LLMS,VideoSafety-R1[32]结合了报警-托肯制导的SFT和安全制导的GPRO,以改善防御推理. 保险 Vid [36]构建视频特定安全偏好数据,并应用直接偏好优化(DPO)[29],而SEA [22]则使用合成模式嵌入,以便从文本数据中实现低资源安全对齐. 补充安全和隐私研究通过VideoJail [8] 和保护性对抗性水印检查视频模式越狱情况,破坏未经授权的视频注释 [18]. 这些指示涉及安全生成、安全反应协调或防止滥用视频投入。 ATPO则通过精细的多标签预测,研究现有视频的温和性.

blocks.en: 3 Proposed Method
blocks.zh: 3 拟议方法

blocks.en: Our training pipeline consists of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) warmup followed by reinforcement learning (RL). We first introduce the task formulation and notation for Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD) (Section 3.1 ). We study different reward formulations, including standard overlap-based rewards (Section 3.2 ) and our proposed Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO) (Section 3.3 ). The overall pipeline is illustrated in Figure 2 .
blocks.zh: 我们的训练管道包括监督的Fine-Tuning(SFT)热身,然后是强化学习(RL)。 我们首先介绍多标签视频安全检测(Multi-VSD)的任务设置和标记(第3.1节)。 我们研究不同的奖励办法,包括基于标准重叠的奖励(第3.2节)和我们提议的适应性的特维尔斯基政策优化(第3.3节)。 整个管道如图2所示。

blocks.en: 3.1 Multi-label Video Safety Detection Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 多标签视频安全检测制剂

blocks.en:
We formulate the task of Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD) by extending previous binary detection. Given a video v v , the model predicts whether the content belongs to any of a predefined set of unsafe categories 𝒞 = { c 1 , … , c K } \mathcal{C}=\{c_{1},\dots,c_{K}\} , where each c c represents a type of harmful content (e.g., violence, misinformation, extremism).
For each video, the model produces a predicted label set P ⊆ 𝒞 P\subseteq\mathcal{C} , while the ground-truth annotation is a label set G ⊆ 𝒞 G\subseteq\mathcal{C} . We denote True Positive (TP), False Positive (FP), and False Negative (FN) as T P = | P ∩ G | , F P = | P ∖ G | , F N = | G ∖ P | . \displaystyle TP=|P\cap G|,\qquad FP=|P\setminus G|,\qquad FN=|G\setminus P|. (1) These quantities characterize the quality of the predicted label set and form the basis of the reward functions used for reinforcement learning and evaluation metrics.

blocks.en: 3.2 GRPO with Static Rewards
blocks.zh: 3.2 有静态奖励的GPRO

blocks.en: Our training follows a two-stage pipeline consisting of SFT warmup followed by RL training, following recent works on post-training VLMs [ 5 , 14 , 49 ] . We first perform SFT on the backbone VLM using a multi-label classification objective, as shown in Figure 2 , where the target outputs correspond to the ground-truth label sets, without auxiliary annotations such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT) [ 37 ] reasoning.
blocks.zh: 我们的训练是继最近关于训练后甚高压材料[5、14、49]的工作之后,由SFT热身和RL训练组成的两阶段的训练。 我们首先使用多标签分类目标在主干VLM上执行SFT,如图2所示,目标输出与地面真实的标签集相对应,没有附加说明如思维链(CoT)[37]推理.

blocks.en:
Following the SFT warmup stage, we further improve the multi-label prediction capability of VLMs using RL training. Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) [ 30 ] is adopted to optimize the model using reward functions defined over predicted and ground-truth label sets.
Given an input video v v and detection instruction x x , the old policy model π θ old \pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}} generates N N sampled outputs { y j } j = 1 N \{y_{j}\}_{j=1}^{N} . blocks.en: 3.3 Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO)
blocks.zh: 3.3 适应性的特维尔斯基政策优化

blocks.en: In practical detection pipelines, different deployment scenarios may require different precision-recall trade-offs. Instead of fixing ( α , β ) (\alpha,\beta) statically, we propose to adapt them dynamically during training so that the model approaches a desired false-negative to false-positive ratio. This leads to our proposed ATPO, which uses a feedback controller that dynamically adjusts the reward function during training. The overall training pipeline is illustrated in Figure 2 . Training first performs SFT warmup, then the model is optimized using ATPO, starting with the GRPO trainer with initialized Tversky coefficients. We instantiate ATPO with two variants of reward formulation. For brevity, we omit the GRPO group notation. The full algorithm is provided in Appendix B .

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: In this section, we evaluate ATPO and the proposed Adaptive Tversky Reward (ATR) on two video safety benchmarks. We first compare our models against large general-purpose VLMs and GRPO with static reward designs. We then analyze ATR’s ability to control the precision-recall trade-off both globally and at the category level, and study the training dynamics of the adaptive controller.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们评价ATPO和拟议的适应性特维尔斯基奖(ATR)两个视频安全基准. 我们首先将我们的模型与大型通用VLM和GPRO与静态奖励设计进行比较. 然后,我们分析ATR在全球和类别层面控制精确召回权衡的能力,并研究适应控制员的培训动态。

blocks.en: 4.1 Experiment Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: Models are evaluated on two public video safety benchmarks: SafeWatch-Bench [ 4 ] and XD-Violence [ 39 ] . SafeWatch-Bench contains 199,604 training videos and 1,420 test videos across six unsafe categories. We use 11,036 full training videos under two minutes for SFT and GRPO, and evaluate on the 820-video SafeWatch-Bench-Real test set. For XD-Violence, we use 3,520 training videos under five minutes and evaluate on the full 800-video test set. Additional dataset statistics, including category co-occurrence, are provided in Appendix C.1 .
blocks.zh: 以两个公共视频安全基准评价模型: 安全观察-奔驰[4]和XD-暴力[39]. 安全观察-奔驰包含199,604个培训视频和1,420个测试视频,分为6个不安全类别. 在SFT和GRPO两分钟内使用11 036个完整训练视频, 对于XD-暴力,我们在5分钟内使用3,520个训练视频,并在完整的800个视频测试集上评价. 附录C.1提供了补充数据集统计数据,包括同一类别统计数据。

blocks.en: We adopt Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct [ 2 ] and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct [ 1 ] as backbone models, both of which support direct video inputs via uniform frame sampling. For the two training stages, SFT is performed with LoRA [ 7 ] using ground-truth safety labels as targets. GRPO training starts from the SFT one-epoch checkpoints and optimizes the reward formulations described in Section 3.2 and 3.3 , together with a small format reward. More implementation details are provided in Appendix C.2 .
blocks.zh: 我们采用Quen2.5-VL-7B-指示[2]和Quen3-VL-8B-指示[1]作为骨干模型,两者都通过统一的帧取样支持直接视频输入. 在两个培训阶段,SFT与LORA[7]一起使用地面-真实安全标签作为目标。 GRPO培训从SFT单一日期的检查站开始,并优化第3.2和3.3节所述的奖励规定,同时提供少量形式的奖励。 附录C.2提供了更多的执行细节。

blocks.en: Four standard multi-label evaluation metrics are reported [ 48 , 34 , 12 ] : Jaccard Index, Micro-F1, Macro-F1, and Binary F1. Jaccard Index measures the intersection-over-union between predicted and ground-truth label sets, as defined in Section 3.2 . Micro-F1 computes F1 after aggregating true positives, false positives, and false negatives across categories, while Macro-F1 averages category-wise F1 scores. Binary F1 collapses all unsafe categories into a single positive class, following prior video safety detection works [ 10 , 20 ] .
blocks.zh: 报告四个标准多标签评价指标[48、34、12]: Jaccard Index, Micro-F1, Macro-F1, 和二进制 F1. Jacard指数衡量第3.2节界定的预测和地面真实标签套之间的交叉。 Micro-F1在将真实的正数,假的正数,以及不同类别的假的负数汇总后计算出F1,而Macro-F1则平均为类智的F1分数. 二进制F1在之前的视频安全检测工程[10,20]之后,将所有不安全的类别都崩溃成单一的正类.

Models are grouped into general-purpose VLMs, video reasoning VLMs, guardrail systems, and our ATPO-trained models with G-ATR and C-ATR. Bold and underlining indicate the best and second-best results. ∗ : further trained on the respective benchmark training sets. † : SafeWatch-8B uses full videos and clips from SafeWatch-Bench.

blocks.en: 4.2 Multi-Label Video Safety Detection Performance
blocks.zh: 4.2 多标签视频安全检测性能

blocks.en: We evaluate several representative VLMs as baselines, including large general-purpose VLMs of different scales from the Qwen-VL and InternVL3.5 families. We also evaluate recent GRPO-trained video reasoning models, Video-R1 [ 5 ] and VideoChat-R1 [ 41 ] , which are built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and trained for general video understanding tasks. Our guardrail baselines include GuardReasoner-VL [ 20 ] , VAD-R1 [ 10 ] , and SafeWatch-8B [ 4 ] , a specialized multi-label video guardrail trained on SafeWatch-Bench.
blocks.zh: 我们评价了几个有代表性的VLM作为基线,包括与Quen-VL和InternVL3.5家族不同规模的大型通用VLM. 我们还评价了最近GRPO训练的视频推理模型,Video-R1[5]和VideoChat-R1[41],这些模型基于Quen2.5-VL-7B,并接受过一般视频理解任务的培训. 我们的护卫铁路基线包括GuardReasoner-VL [20],VAD-R1 [10],以及SafeWatch-8B [4],这是在SafeWatch-Bench上训练的专用多标签视频护卫铁路.

blocks.en: Evaluation results for baseline models, prior work, and our models on SafeWatch-Bench-Real and XD-Violence are reported in Table 1 . Our models are denoted as ATPO-G and ATPO-C, corresponding to ATPO trained with G-ATR and C-ATR, respectively, and are based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B backbones. The results reveal several key findings.
blocks.zh: 表1报告了基线模型、前期工作以及我们的安全观察-Bench-Real和XD-暴力模型的评价结果。 我们的型号表示为ATPO-G型和ATPO-C型,对应分别经过G-ATR和C-ATR训练的ATPO型,并以Qun2.5-VL-7B和Qun3-VL-8B型骨干为基础. 调查结果揭示了几个关键的调查结果。

blocks.en: Multi-VSD remains challenging. Even very large VLMs (row 4 and row 5) still achieve only moderate Multi-VSD performance on SafeWatch-Bench-Real (Jaccard < 61 <61 ), despite relatively strong binary detection (Binary F1 > 85 >85 ). In contrast, most models obtain consistently higher scores on XD-Violence, suggesting XD-Violence is an easier benchmark under the evaluation metrics. Notably, models trained with GRPO for general video reasoning do not yield substantial gains. Video-R1 (row 6) and VideoChat-R1 (row 7) both build on the Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone. Compared to the backbone’s results (row 1), Video-R1 shows no improvement (Jaccard 39.99 39.99 vs. 40.66 40.66 ), and VideoChat-R1 provides only a modest gain (Jaccard 44.20 44.20 vs. 40.66 40.66 ). This indicates that general video reasoning training alone is insufficient for Multi-VSD, and that dedicated in-domain training is likely necessary.
blocks.zh: 多重VSD仍然具有挑战性。 即使是非常大的VLM(第4行和第5行)在Safe Watch-Bench-Real(Jaccard < 61 < 61)上仍然只实现了中等的多VSD性能,尽管相对强大的二进制检测(Binary F1 > 85 > 85). 相比之下,大多数模型在XD-暴力上得到的分数一直较高,这表明XD-暴力在评价指标下是一个比较容易的基准. 值得注意的是,经过GRPO培训的一般视频推理模式没有取得实质性成果。 Video-R1(第6卷)和VideoChat-R1(第7卷)都建立在Quen2.5-VL-7B主干线上. 与骨干成果(第1行)相比,Video-R1没有改善(Jaccard 39.99 39.99 vs 40.66 40.66),Video. Chat-R1只提供了微薄的收益(Jaccard 44.20 44.20 vs 40.66 40.66 . 这表明,光是一般的视频推理培训不足以用于多维软件开发,而且可能有必要进行专门的国内培训。

blocks.en: ATPO improves Multi-VSD performance. ATPO substantially improves Multi-VSD performance over the backbone models. For Qwen2.5-VL-7B, G-ATR and C-ATR (rows 12-13) improve SafeWatch-Bench-Real Jaccard from 40.66 40.66 (row 1) to 75.44 75.44 / 75.15 75.15 (a ∼ \sim + 35 35 point gain). For Qwen3-VL-8B, G-ATR and C-ATR (rows 14-15) improve Jaccard from 48.69 48.69 (row 3) to 75.50 75.50 / 74.63 74.63 . Overall, ATPO-trained models substantially outperform both larger general-purpose VLMs and video reasoning VLMs based on the same backbone model.
blocks.zh: ATPO改进了多VSD的性能. ATPO比骨干模型大大提高了多VSD的性能. 对于Qun2.5-VL-7B,G-ATR和C-ATR(12-13行),Safe Watch-Bench-Real Jacard从40.66 40.66(1行)改进为75.44 75.44 75.44 75.15 75.15 (a \sim + 35 35 点增益). 对于Qune3-VL-8B,G-ATR和C-ATR(第14-15行),Jaccard从48.69 48.69(第3行)改进为75.50 75.50/74.63 74.63. 总体而言,ATPO训练的模型在基于同一主干模型的更大通用VLM和视频推理VLM上都大大超过表现.

blocks.en: ATPO outperforms specialized guardrails. SafeWatch-8B (row 11) provides a strong in-domain baseline, achieving the best non-ATPO results across all four metrics on SafeWatch-Bench-Real. Nevertheless, all four ATPO variants outperform SafeWatch-8B across all eight dataset-metric combinations. In particular, ATPO-G-7B achieves Jaccard scores of 75.44 75.44 and 88.17 88.17 on SafeWatch-Bench-Real and XD-Violence, compared with 70.69 70.69 and 79.84 79.84 for SafeWatch-8B, corresponding to gains of 4.75 4.75 and 8.33 8.33 points. In Appendix H we also show that ATPO outperforms SafeWatch-8B and other training baselines on videos with multiple labels only.
blocks.zh: ATPO的表现优于专业的护栏. Safe Watch-8B(第11行)提供了一个强大的域内基线,在Safe Watch-Bench-Real上的所有四个度量标准上都取得了最佳的非ATPO结果. 尽管如此,在所有8个数据集计量组合中,所有4个ATPO变体都超过了安全观察-8B。 特别是,ATPO-G-7B在安全观察-Bench-Real和XD-violence上的Jaccard分数分别为75.4475.44和88.1788.17,而安全观察-8B的分数则为70.6970.69和79.8479.84,分别是4.754.75和8.338.33分。 在附录H中,我们还显示,ATPO在仅具有多个标签的视频上的表现超过了安全观察-8B和其他培训基线.

blocks.en: Besides Multi-VSD, ATPO-trained models also excel at binary classification. All ATPO-trained models achieve Binary F1 > 93 >93 on both datasets (rows 12-15), indicating that optimizing for multi-label safety detection also leads to strong binary safety detection performance. Notably, the binary performance of these models is higher than guardrail models that are trained specifically for binary detection. Another finding from the results is that G-ATR and C-ATR have comparable overall performance. Across both backbones, G-ATR and C-ATR are very close (rows 12 vs. 13 and rows 14 vs. 15), with minor trade-offs across metrics. This suggests robustness to the choice of global vs. category-wise control in our ATPO training.
blocks.zh: 除多VSD外,ATPO训练的模型在二进制分类方面也非常出色. 所有ATPO训练过的模型在两个数据集上都实现了二进制F1 > 93>93(第12-15行),表明优化多标签安全检测也会导致强大的二进制安全检测性能. 值得注意的是,这些模型的二进制性能高于专门为二进制检测而训练的护栏模型. 结果得出的另一项结论是,G-ATR和C-ATR具有可比较的总体业绩。 纵观两条主干线,G-ATR和C-ATR非常接近(12对13,第14对15行),在跨度量衡上略有权衡. 这表明,在我们ATPO的训练中,全球对照类别控制的选择是强有力的。

blocks.en: Overall, Table 1 presents our best results using in-domain training with ATPO, showing substantial improvements over zero-shot general-purpose models. We further examine transfer across the SafeWatch-Bench and XD-Violence taxonomies, including adaptation with only 10 % 10\% of the target training data, in Appendix L . In the subsequent table, we show the relative contributions of our in-domain training techniques.
blocks.zh: 总体而言,表1介绍了我们利用与ATPO的域内培训取得的最佳成果,显示比零镜头通用模型有了很大的改进。 我们进一步审查安全观察-奔驰和XD-暴力分类之间的转移,包括附录L中只有10%的目标培训数据的适应。 在随后的表格中,我们显示了我们国内培训技术的相对贡献。

blocks.en: 4.3 Comparison of Static and Adaptive Reward Optimization
blocks.zh: 4.3 静态和适应性奖励优化比较

blocks.en: Table 2 compares zero-shot evaluation, SFT, GRPO with static rewards (EM and STR), and ATPO with adaptive rewards (G-ATR and C-ATR), using Qwen2.5-VL-7B. We evaluate on both the real and AI-generated test subsets of SafeWatch-Bench [ 4 ] , referred to as Real and GenAI below.

blocks.en: ATPO substantially improves over its initialization. Starting from SFT-1ep, ATPO-G and ATPO-C improve Real Jaccard from 44.33 44.33 to 75.15 75.15 , respectively, corresponding to gains of 31.11 31.11 and 30.82 30.82 points. GenAI Jaccard also increases from 66.34 66.34 to 74.29 74.29 and 73.35 73.35 , respectively. Both variants improve all four metrics on both subsets relative to their shared initialization.
blocks.zh: ATPO在初始化之后有了很大的改进. 从SFT-1ep开始,ATPO-G和ATPO-C将Real Jacard分别从44.33 44.33升至75.15 75.15升至30.82分。 GenAI Jacard也分别从66.34 66.34增至74.29 74.29和73.35 73.35。 这两个变体相对于共同初始化,改进了两个子集上的所有四个度量.

blocks.en: Extended SFT trades off Real and GenAI performance. AI-generated videos are less represented in the SafeWatch-Bench training set compared to real videos. Extending SFT from one to three epochs increases Real Jaccard from 44.33 44.33 to 67.93 67.93 , but reduces GenAI Jaccard from 66.34 66.34 to 62.32 62.32 . GenAI Micro and Binary F1 also decline. Thus, the gains from extended SFT do not hold across both video types. In contrast, both ATPO variants outperform SFT-3ep across all four metrics on both subsets. Cross-dataset evaluation on VHD11K-Video [ 43 ] shows a similar pattern for extended SFT and ATPO-C (Appendix G ).
blocks.zh: 扩展的SFT与Real和GenAI的性能进行交易. AI制作的视频在Safe Watch-Bench的训练集中与真实的视频相比表现较少. 将 SFT 从一个时代延长到三个时代 真正的Jaccard从44.33 44.33降至67.93 67.93,但将GenAI Jaccard从66.34 66.34降至62.32 62.32. GenAI Micro和二进制F1也有所下降. 因此,扩展的SFT带来的收益并不涵盖两种视频类型。 相比之下,两个ATPO的变体在两个子集的所有四个度量中都超过了SFT-3ep的性能. VHD11K-Video的跨数据集评价[43]显示了扩展的SFT和ATPO-C(附录G)的类似模式.

blocks.en: Adaptive rewards outperform static rewards. Among the static rewards, STR achieves higher Jaccard than EM on both subsets, consistent with the benefit of graded feedback for partially correct predictions. Both ATPO variants further outperform EM and STR across all eight dataset-metric combinations. Relative to GRPO with STR, ATPO-G improves Jaccard by 5.35 5.35 on Real ( 70.09 70.09 to 75.44 75.44 ) and 5.17 5.17 points on GenAI ( 69.12 69.12 to 74.29 74.29 ). ATPO-C achieves corresponding gains of 5.06 5.06 and 4.23 4.23 points. These matched-RL comparisons support the contribution of adaptive reward design and suggest that adaptively rebalancing FN/FP during training provides a more informative learning signal than EM or STR (qualitative analysis in Appendix I ). Moreover, while SFT and static rewards impose a fixed operating point, ATR enables stable RL optimization with controllable error trade-offs, which we examine in the next section. Additional Qwen3-VL-8B results are provided in Appendix F .
blocks.zh: 适应性奖励优于静态奖励. 在静态奖励中,STR在两个子集上都实现了高于EM的Jaccard,这与分级反馈对部分正确预测的好处是一致的. ATPO两个变体在所有八个数据集计量组合中都进一步超过了EM和STR。 与STRA的GRPO相比,ATPO-G在Real上改进了5.355.35(70.09至75.44 75.44),在GenAI上改进了5.175.17分(69.12至74.29 74.29)。 ATPO-C实现相应增益5.065.06和4.234.23分. 这些对应的RL比较支持适应性奖励设计的贡献,并表明在培训期间适应性地重新平衡新军/新军/新军,比EM或STR(附录一的定性分析)提供了更丰富的学习信号。 此外,虽然SFT和静态的奖励强制规定一个固定的操作点,但ATR通过可控误差权衡可以实现稳定的RL优化,我们在下一节对此进行考察. 附录F提供了额外的Quen3-VL-8B结果。

blocks.en: 4.4.1 Global Control via G-ATR
blocks.zh: 4.4.1 通过G-ATR进行全球控制

blocks.en: To quantify global control, we report micro Precision (P), micro Recall (R), and their ratio P/R in Table 3 . We additionally report Error Type Ratio (ETR), defined as FN/FP, which directly measures the relative prevalence of type-II errors (false negatives) vs. type-I errors (false positives). For G-ATR, we vary the target ratio r ∗ r^{*} : a smaller r ∗ r^{*} is expected to suppress FN and thus encourage a recall-dominant operating point, whereas a larger r ∗ r^{*} should suppress FP and shift the model toward a precision-dominant regime. For comparison, we evaluate the Static Tversky Reward (STR) defined in Equation 6 , where the coefficients α \alpha and β \beta are fixed. Under STR, a smaller α / β \alpha/\beta places greater penalty on FN, while a larger α / β \alpha/\beta penalizes FP more. We make the following two observations from Table 3 .
blocks.zh: 为了量化全球控制,我们在表3中报告了微精度(P)、微量召回(R)及其比例。 我们另外报告错误类型比率(ETR),定义为FN/FP,它直接测量II类错误(假负数)相对于I类错误(假正数)的相对流行率. 对于G-ATR,我们改变目标比率r * r : 预期较小的r r r 将压制新军,从而鼓励一个召回式的操作点,而较大的r r r 将压制FP,并将模型转向精确的支配性制度。 为了比较起见,我们评价了第6项中定义的静态特维尔斯基奖励(STR),其中的系数α\α和β\β是固定的. 根据《可疑交易报告》,较小的α /β α /\β β /\β 对新军的处罚更大,而较大的α /β α /\β β 处罚更重。 我们从表3中提出以下两点意见。

blocks.en: G-ATR yields monotonic global control. Across the full sweep of target ratios, G-ATR produces a clear and monotonic progression in the achieved precision-recall ratio. As r ∗ r^{*} increases, precision increases while recall decreases, and the achieved P/R rises steadily from 0.77 ​ ( r ∗ = 0.2 ) 0.77(r^{*}=0.2) to 1.16 ​ ( r ∗ = 5 ) 1.16(r^{*}=5) . Notably, ETR follows the same intended direction: as r ∗ r^{*} grows, FN/FP increases monotonically from 0.31 0.31 to 1.75 1.75 . Overall, varying r ∗ r^{*} smoothly shifts the model from a recall-favoring regime to a precision-favoring regime, suggesting that G-ATR functions as a stable feedback controller for global steering. The corresponding precision–recall curves are provided in Appendix D . In contrast, we find that STR does not provide reliable control under fixed FN and FP weightings. The achieved P/R under STR is non-monotonic and sometimes moves counter to the desired direction as α / β \alpha/\beta increases. The lack of consistency is further reflected by ETR, which does not exhibit a clean monotonic relationship with α / β \alpha/\beta . This instability indicates that simply fixing the ratio α β \frac{\alpha}{\beta} is insufficient for predictable global precision-recall steering during GRPO training. We additionally compare ATPO-G with post-hoc threshold tuning of SFT and GRPO (STR) in Appendix K .

blocks.en: 4.4.2 Category-Level Control via C-ATR
blocks.zh: 4.4.2 通过C-ATR进行类别控制

blocks.en: To evaluate category-level control, we select the two strongest general-purpose models from Table 1 , InternVL3.5-38B and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B, as reference models. We focus on C4 ( Misinformation ) and C6 ( Extreme ) because misinformation detection may prioritize higher precision to reduce over-censorship, whereas extreme content prioritizes higher recall to minimize harmful exposure. We report category-wise Precision, Recall, P/R, and ETR on SafeWatch-Bench-Real in Table 4 .

blocks.en:
Over-conservative behavior of large VLMs . We find that large VLMs exhibit high-precision, low-recall "over-conservative" behavior. Both InternVL and Qwen3-VL show conservative behavior on both C4 and C6. They achieve very high precision ( > 94 >94 ) but low recall ( < 23 <23 ), resulting in disproportionately large P/R and very high ETR values. This indicates that, without task-specific alignment, even highly capable models tend not to flag these two evaluated categories, leading to many missed harmful videos. In comparison, C-ATR enables controllable, category-level precision-recall trade-offs. The controlled setting ( r 4 ∗ = 5.0 , r 6 ∗ = 0.2 r^{*}_{4}=5.0,r^{*}_{6}=0.2 ) demonstrates the desired asymmetric steering: C4 shifts toward higher precision (from 55.28 55.28 to 70.41 70.41 ), while C6 shifts toward high recall ( 79.07 79.07 to 94.57 94.57 ). Overall, these results show that C-ATR can override the "overly conservative" zero-shot behavior and provide practical, category-aware operating points aligned with heterogeneous safety requirements. blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduced ATPO, an adaptive reward framework for multi-label harmful video detection that enables controllable precision–recall trade-offs during RL training. Experiments show that ATPO improves multi-label detection while maintaining strong binary safety performance. Furthermore, ATPO provides a flexible mechanism for aligning model behavior with different moderation policies by adjusting the desired precision–recall operating point.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们引入了ATPO,这是一个适应性的奖励框架,用于多标签有害视频检测,在RL训练中可以控制精度-回顾权衡。 实验显示,ATPO改进了多标签检测,同时保持强大的二元安全性能. 此外,ATPO通过调整所期望的精确性-召回操作点,为模型行为与不同的温和政策搭配提供了灵活的机制.

blocks.en: Appendix A Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录A

blocks.en: Our evaluation follows the category definitions and annotations provided by existing benchmarks (e.g., SafeWatch-Bench and XD-Violence), which reflect commonly adopted operational definitions of harmful content. However, the boundaries of categories such as misinformation, violence, or extremism may vary across cultural, legal, and platform-specific contexts. As a result, model behavior may differ under alternative definitions or policies. While ATPO provides a mechanism to adjust error trade-offs, adapting to different definitions may require dataset-specific annotation and validation.
blocks.zh: 我们的评价遵循现有基准(例如安全观察-奔驰和XD-暴力)提供的类别定义和说明,这些基准反映了通常采用的有害内容的业务定义。 然而,错误信息、暴力或极端主义等类别的界限可能因文化、法律和平台的具体情况而异。 因此,模型行为在替代定义或政策下可能有所不同. 虽然ATPO提供了一个调整错误权衡的机制,但适应不同定义可能需要针对数据集的注释和验证.

blocks.en: ATPO enables controllable precision-recall trade-offs, but selecting appropriate target ratios requires application-specific tuning and validation. In particular, different operating points may lead to over-moderation (false positives) or missed harmful content (false negatives). Therefore, ATPO is best used as an assistive component in moderation pipelines to support human decision-making rather than serving as a fully automated standalone system.
blocks.zh: ATPO能够实现可控制的精确召回权衡,但选择适当的目标比率需要应用特定的调试和验证. 特别是,不同的操作点可能导致超调(假阳性)或漏掉有害内容(假阴性). 因此,ATPO最好用作温和管道中的辅助部分,以支持人类决策,而不是作为一个完全自动化的独立系统。

blocks.en: In Section 3.3 , we present the training pipeline of Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO). Here we provide the full training procedure of ATPO instantiated with the Category-Aware Adaptive Tversky Reward (C-ATR) in Algorithm 1 . The training begins with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to initialize the Vision-Language Model (VLM) with harmful category definitions. ATPO then iteratively performs GRPO rollouts and policy updates [ 30 ] , followed by EMA updates, ratio estimation, and controller updates that adapt the Tversky coefficients [ 35 ] toward the target ratios.

blocks.en: In Section 4.1 , we introduce the two test sets used for evaluation: SafeWatch-Bench-Real [ 4 ] and XD-Violence [ 39 ] . Here we present additional dataset statistics to illustrate the characteristics of these datasets and the challenges they pose for Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD). Table 5 shows the distribution of samples with each harmful category and multi-label samples among all unsafe samples. We can see that the proportion of multi-label videos is substantially higher in SafeWatch-Bench-Real (25.52%) than in XD-Violence (9.40%). This indicates that SafeWatch more frequently contains videos exhibiting multiple harmful categories simultaneously, which increases prediction ambiguity and helps explain the greater difficulty observed for SafeWatch in Section 4.2 . This highlights the importance of methods that can reliably handle multi-label predictions. In addition, XD-Violence exhibits notable category imbalance, with the Abuse category accounting for only 2.2% of unsafe samples. Such imbalance could make it difficult for models to maintain consistent precision–recall trade-offs across categories.
blocks.zh: 在第4.1节中,我们介绍了用于评价的两套测试: 安全观察-奔驰-真实[4]和XD-暴力[39]. 在此,我们提出更多的数据集统计数据,以说明这些数据集的特点及其对多标签视频安全检测(Multi-VSD)构成的挑战。 表5显示所有不安全样本中含有每个有害类别和多标签样本的样本分布情况。 与XD-暴力(9.40%)相比, 这表明, " 安全观察 " 更经常地包含同时显示多种有害类别的视频,这增加了预测的模糊性,并有助于解释第4.2节中观察到的 " 安全观察 " 的更大困难。 这突出了可靠处理多标签预测的方法的重要性。 此外,XD-暴力显示出明显的类别不平衡,虐待类别只占不安全样本的2.2%。 这种不平衡可能使模型难以保持一致的准确性,难以在类别之间相互回顾权衡。

blocks.en: Figure 3 further illustrates the relationships between categories by showing the category co-occurrence matrices for unsafe samples in the two test sets. We can see that several categories frequently co-occur in SafeWatch-Bench-Real, such as C3 ( Violence ) with C5 ( Illegal ) and C6 ( Extreme ), whereas category overlap in XD-Violence is generally more limited. These patterns highlight the inherently multi-label nature of harmful videos, which motivates the development of ATPO for Multi-VSD.

blocks.en: C.2 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: C.2 执行细节

blocks.en: Figure 4 : Prompt template used during ATPO training and inference on SafeWatch-Bench. Detailed descriptions of harmful categories are omitted for brevity.
blocks.zh: 图4:ATPO培训和关于安全观察-奔驰的推论中使用的快速模板。 为简洁起见,略去对有害类别的详细说明。

blocks.en: Video Processing. Videos are processed using the official preprocessing pipeline qwen-vl-utils [ 2 , 1 ] . Frames are sampled at 1 frame per second (FPS) without enforcing a fixed number of frames per video, so the sequence length varies with video duration. Frames are sampled uniformly across the video. Each frame is resized using dynamic resolution while preserving the original aspect ratio.
blocks.zh: 视频处理. 视频使用官方预处理管道qwen-vl-utils[2,1]进行处理. 帧按每秒1帧(FPS)进行采样,不执行每个视频固定的帧数,因此序列长度随视频持续时间而变化. 录像上对框架进行统一取样。 每个框架都使用动态分辨率进行调整,同时保留原有的宽比.

blocks.en: Prompt Format. The model receives a task instruction describing the video safety detection objective together with the category definitions. The prompt instructs the model to provide reasoning and output the predicted safety categories in a structured format following the original prompt used in SafeWatch-Bench [ 4 ] . The exact prompt template used during ATPO training and inference on SafeWatch-Bench is provided in Figure 4 .
blocks.zh: 提示格式 。 该模型收到任务指令,说明视频安全检测目标以及类别定义. 即时指示模型提供推理,并按照SafeWatch-Bench [4]中最初使用的即时提示,以结构化格式输出预测的安全类别. 图4提供了ATPO培训和关于安全观察-奔驰的推论中使用的准确的快速模板。

blocks.en: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT). Training begins with an SFT stage to align the base VLM with the Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD) task. The SFT stage is trained for 1 epoch on the training split of each dataset using the standard language modeling objective. Additional hyperparameters follow common VLM fine-tuning practices, including the optimizer AdamW [ 21 ] , learning rate = 10 − 5 =10^{-5} , effective batch size = 8 =8 , and maximum sequence length = 24576 =24576 . The LoRA rank is set to 64 and the scaling factor is set to 128.
blocks.zh: 监督精通(SFT). 训练从一个SFT阶段开始,使基础VLM与多标签视频安全检测(Multi-VSD)任务一致. SFT阶段是利用标准语言建模目标对每个数据集进行分解培训的一个时代。 附加的超参数遵循常见的VLM微调操作,包括优化器AdamW [21],学习率=10−5=10×5}有效批量大小=8×8,最大序列长度=24576×24576. LORA等级为64级,缩放系数为128级.

blocks.en: Reinforcement Learning Training. After SFT, we further optimize the model using the proposed ATPO framework. The RL stage runs for 3 epochs. For each input sample, the model generates a group of responses to estimate policy advantages. The key RL hyperparameters are: group size = 8 =8 , sampling temperature = 1.0 =1.0 , top- p = 1.0 p=1.0 , and KL penalty coefficient β KL = 10 − 2 \beta_{\mathrm{KL}}=10^{-2} . The reference policy is the SFT-initialized model. For the ATPO controller, we use controller step size η = 0.01 \eta=0.01 , EMA smoothing factor λ = 0.95 \lambda=0.95 , and stability constant ε = 10 − 8 \varepsilon=10^{-8} . These parameters are shared across both the global and category-level variants of ATR.
blocks.zh: 加强学习培训。 在SFT之后,我们利用拟议的ATPO框架进一步优化模型. RL舞台运行时间为3个纪元. 对于每个输入样本,模型生成一组用于估计政策优势的响应. 关键RL超参数为:组大小=8=8,采样温度=1.0=1.0,顶-p=1.0p=1.0,KL罚分系数βKL=10−2\beta_{\mathrm{KL}}=10^{-2}. 参考政策是SFT初始化模式. 对于ATPO控制器,我们使用控制器的步数大小 = 0.01\eta= 0.01,EMA平滑系数 = 0.95\lambda= 0.95,稳定性常数 = 10− 8\varepsilon= 10×8}. 这些参数在ATR的全球性和类级变体之间都有共享.

blocks.en: Training Infrastructure. All experiments are conducted on four NVIDIA H800 80GB GPUs. Training is performed using BF16 mixed-precision. The following libraries/packages were used for implementing the experiments: LLaMA-Factory [ 51 ] , a modified version of EasyR1 [ 50 ] , PyTorch 2.8.0 , vLLM 0.11.0 , Transformers 4.57.3 , and CUDA 12.8 . On average, RL training for three epochs takes approximately 20 hours on our GPU cluster.
blocks.zh: 培训基础设施。 所有实验都是在四个NVIDIA H800 80GB GPU上进行的. 培训使用BF16混合精度。 以下库/包用于实施实验: LLaMA-Factory [51],经过修改的EasyR1 [50],PyTorch 2.8.0,vLLM 0.11.0,变形器 4.57.3,和CUDA 12.8. 平均来说,三个纪元的RL训练需要我们GPU集群大约20小时.

blocks.en: C.3 Prior Work
blocks.zh: C.3 先前的工作

blocks.en: We compare ATPO with recent approaches exploring Reinforcement Learning (RL) and reasoning capabilities in VLMs for video understanding and safety detection. Here we provide a more detailed description of those approaches that we evaluate in Section 4.2 .
blocks.zh: 我们比较了ATPO与最近探索加强学习(RL)的方法和VLM的推理能力,以进行视频理解和安全检测. 在此,我们更详细地说明我们在第4.2节中评价的那些办法。

blocks.en: GuardReasoner-VL. GuardReasoner-VL [ 20 ] proposes a reasoning-based VLM guardrail model for multi-modal safety moderation. The model is trained to generate an explicit reasoning process before producing moderation decisions. The model is first initialized with reasoning SFT and then further optimized with online GRPO using a length-aware safety reward. Although the original GuardReasoner-VL is trained and evaluated on text, image, and text-image data rather than video, its backbone model, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, supports direct video inputs. Therefore, we evaluate GuardReasoner-VL on video inputs in our experiments for comparison with other models.
blocks.zh: 卫视Reasoner-VL. GuardReasoner-VL [20] 提出了基于推理的VLM护卫模型,用于多式联运安全节制. 该模式经过培训,在作出温和决定之前,可以产生明确的推理过程。 该型号首先以推理SFT初始化,然后使用长知安全奖励与在线GPRO进一步优化. 虽然最初的Guard Reasoner-VL在文本,图像,文本图像数据而不是视频上接受了培训和评价,但其骨干模型Quen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct支持直接视频输入. 因此,我们评价GuardReasoner-VL在我们实验中的视频投入,以便与其他模型进行比较。

blocks.en: VAD-R1. VAD-R1 [ 10 ] proposes a reinforcement-learning-based framework for Video Anomaly Reasoning (VAR) that encourages VLMs to perform structured reasoning when analyzing anomalous events in videos. The model is trained using a two-stage pipeline: after initial supervised alignment, the model is optimized using Anomaly Verification Augmented GRPO (AVA-GRPO). AVA-GRPO extends GRPO with an anomaly verification reward that re-evaluates predictions by performing reasoning on temporally trimmed versions of the video. In our experiments, we further train VAD-R1 on the training set of SafeWatch-Bench using AVA-GRPO and report the evaluation results in Section 4.2 .
blocks.zh: VAD-R1. VAD-R1 [10] 提出了视频异常理性(VAR)的强化学习框架,鼓励VLM在分析视频异常事件时进行结构化推理. 该模型使用两阶段的管道进行训练:在初始监督对齐后,该模型使用异常验证增强型GRPO(AVA-GRPO)进行优化. AVA-GRPO将GRPO扩展为异常的验证奖励,通过对视频的暂时修剪版本进行推理来重新评价预测. 在我们的实验中,我们利用AVA-GRPO,对VAD-R1进行安全观察-Bench培训,并在第4.2节中报告评价结果。

blocks.en:
Video-R1 and VideoChat-R1. Video-R1 [ 5 ] extends the R1-style rule-based RL paradigm to video understanding by introducing Temporal Group Relative Policy Optimization (T-GRPO), a variant of GRPO designed to encourage general temporal reasoning over video frames. T-GRPO contrasts model performance on temporally ordered versus randomly shuffled frame sequences.
VideoChat-R1 [ 15 ] investigates reinforcement fine-tuning of video VLMs using GRPO with task-specific spatio-temporal rewards. The training incorporates reward functions tailored to several video perception tasks, including temporal grounding and video question answering, enabling the model to improve spatio-temporal perception while maintaining general dialogue capabilities.
blocks.zh:
Video-R1和VideoChat-R1. Video-R1[5]通过引入Tempolar Group相对政策优化(T-GRPO),将R1风格的规则RL范式扩展至视频理解,这是GRPO的一个变体,旨在鼓励一般时间推理超越视频帧. T-GRPO对比了按时序排列的模型性能与随机排列的帧序列.
VideoChat-R1 [15] 调查加强视频VLM使用GRPO进行微调,并带有特定任务时段奖赏. 培训包含一些针对视频感知任务的奖励功能,包括时间定位和视频问答,使该模式能够在保持一般对话能力的同时改善时空感知。

blocks.en: SafeWatch-8B. SafeWatch-8B [ 4 ] is a video guardrail model built on InternVL2-8B that produces multi-label safety decisions and content-specific explanation conditioned on safety policies. It introduces Parallel Equivalent Policy Encoding (PEPE) to encode policies independently and Policy-Aware Adaptive Pruning (PAP) to retain policy-relevant visual tokens. Its training pipeline comprises multi-task supervised fine-tuning, guardrail-specific fine-tuning with pruning on SafeWatch-Bench, and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) [ 29 ] to improve explanations and reduce false positives. We include SafeWatch-8B as a specialized multi-label video guardrail baseline in Table 1 .

blocks.en: We investigate the effects of the step size η \eta , which determines how strongly the current log-ratio error contributes to the update of u t + 1 u_{t+1} in Equation 9 . Figure 6 shows the evolution of ETR (FN/FP) on a small validation set as training proceeds under different step sizes η \eta . The target ratio is fixed at r ∗ = 1.0 r^{*}=1.0 (dashed horizontal line). Overall, we find that ATPO steers the model toward the target ratio. Across all four settings, ETR starts above the target, indicating a recall-dominant regime. As training progresses, ATPO drives ETR downward toward the target of 1. This suggests that ATPO effectively behaves as a feedback controller, guiding the model toward the specified target. η \eta controls controller responsiveness. For larger η \eta (0.2, 0.1), ETR decreases rapidly during early training, which indicates faster convergence and stronger reaction to deviations from the target. However, this stronger control introduces noticeable oscillations. η = 0.2 \eta=0.2 exhibits larger fluctuations after approaching the target compared to η = 0.1 \eta=0.1 . In contrast, for small η \eta (0.05, 0.01), ETR decreases more gradually and convergence takes longer. The resulting trajectories are smoother with dampened oscillations, suggesting better stability of the controller. This indicates that η \eta determines how aggressively the controller reacts to instantaneous error. These effects of η \eta align with the behavior of a step size parameter in learning and feedback control.

blocks.en: Appendix I Qualitative Analysis

blocks.en: In this section, we provide qualitative comparisons between models trained with GRPO (STR) and our ATPO framework in Figure 7 . Across these examples, the GRPO (STR) model tends to focus on a single salient aspect of the scene, which can lead to missed categories or incorrect interpretations, while ATPO-trained models produce more comprehensive reasoning and more accurate predictions. In the first case, the video shows a robbery taking place inside a shop. The individuals are attempting to break the display glass while pointing a gun at an employee. The GRPO (STR) model focuses on the theft aspect and predicts only the Illegal category while overlooking the violence (shooting) involved. ATPO (G-ATR), on the other hand, recognizes both the illegal activity and the violent threat, resulting in correct predictions. In the second case, the video shows a dog walker abusing a dog in an elevator, which is labeled as Abuse . The GRPO (STR) model produces uncertain reasoning and incorrectly predicts Violence , missing the correct Abuse category. In contrast, ATPO (G-ATR) correctly identifies the behavior as abuse toward the animal and predicts the appropriate category. In the third case, the video depicts a military knife training scenario labeled as Violence and Extreme (with a subcategory of incitement to violence ). The GRPO model interprets the scene as routine training and therefore dismisses the possibility that the content may reflect or promote harmful or extremist activity. In contrast, the ATPO (C-ATR) model produces reasoning that acknowledges the potentially violent nature of the activity and its potential to glorify violence. These examples suggest that ATPO can encourage more comprehensive reasoning about harmful content within videos, enabling the model to capture multiple unsafe aspects or correctly interpret the nature of the behavior, thereby reducing missed labels in Multi-VSD.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们提供了与GPRO(STRA)和我们ATPO框架在图7中培训的模型之间的定性比较。 在这些例子中,GRPO(STR)模型往往侧重于场景的一个突出方面,这可能导致错失类别或错误解释,而ATPO训练的模型则产生更全面的推理和更准确的预测. 在第一起案件中,录像显示在一家商店内发生了一起抢劫事件。 这些人试图在用枪指着一名雇员时打破展示玻璃。 GRPO模式侧重于盗窃方面,只预测非法类别,而忽略所涉暴力(射击)。 另一方面,ATPO(G-ATR)认识到非法活动和暴力威胁,从而得出正确的预测。 在第二起案件中,录像显示一个狗行者在电梯里虐待一只狗,被贴上虐待标签。 GPRO(STR)模式产生不确定的推理,并错误地预测暴力,缺少正确的虐待类别. 反之,ATPO(G-ATR)正确地将行为确定为对动物的虐待,并预测了适当的类别. 在第三个案例中,录像描绘了一个军事刀训练场景,被标注为暴力和极端(有一个煽动暴力的子类别)。 GRPO模式将现场解释为常规训练,因此排除了内容可能反映或促进有害或极端主义活动的可能性. 相反,ATPO(C-ATR)模式产生了一些推理,承认该活动具有潜在的暴力性质及其美化暴力的潜力。 这些例子表明ATPO可以鼓励对视频中有害内容进行更全面的推理,使模型能够捕捉到多个不安全方面或正确解释行为的性质,从而减少多VSD中错失的标签.

blocks.en: Appendix N Societal Impacts
blocks.zh: 附录N 社会影响

blocks.en: The proposed ATPO framework is designed to improve automated detection of unsafe content in videos, thereby assisting human moderators in identifying potentially harmful material across multiple categories, such as violence, illegal activities, misinformation, and extremist content. The system is intended to support research on video safety and contribute to the development of more reliable moderation tools for online platforms. In particular, its controllable precision-recall behavior may help adapt detection systems to different deployment requirements, where some scenarios require higher recall to reduce harmful exposure, while others require higher precision to avoid unnecessary intervention.
blocks.zh: 拟议的ATPO框架旨在改进对视频中不安全内容的自动检测,从而协助人类主持人识别各种可能有害的材料,如暴力、非法活动、错误信息和极端主义内容。 该系统旨在支持视频安全研究,并有助于为在线平台开发更可靠的节制工具。 特别是,其可控制的精密召回行为可能有助于使检测系统适应不同的部署要求,有些情景需要更高的召回才能减少有害的接触,而另一些情景则需要更高的精确度以避免不必要的干预.

blocks.en: However, ATPO is not intended to replace human judgment in high-stakes moderation decisions. Its outputs should be used as supporting signals within broader moderation pipelines rather than as final decisions. We believe that improving the reliability and controllability of multi-label video safety detection can contribute positively to online safety by helping moderation systems identify unsafe content more effectively and efficiently.
blocks.zh: 然而,ATPO并不是为了在高调的温和决定中取代人类的判断. 其产出应用作更广泛的温和管道中的辅助信号,而不是最后决定。 我们认为,提高多标签视频安全检测的可靠性和可控性,能够通过帮助温和系统更有效和高效地识别不安全内容,积极促进在线安全。

blocks.en:
1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Please refer to the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Please see Appendix A . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not include formal theoretical results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide a detailed description of our ATPO algorithm in Section 3 and Appendix B , and details of the experimental setup in Section 4.1 and Appendix C . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide details of the environment in Appendix C and will provide code and scripts upon publication. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We describe datasets, splits, models, evaluation metrics, training procedure, and key hyperparameters in Section 4.1 and Appendix C . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No] Justification: We note that conducting multiple training runs would require substantially greater computational cost. We found that results are consistent across models and datasets (Section 4.2 , 4.3 , and 4.4 ). Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide the information in Appendix C.2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Answer: [Yes] Justification: Our research has been conducted with strict adherence to the NeurIPS Code of
Ethics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Please see Appendix N . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 请参看摘要、导言和结论。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 请见附录A。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文件不包括正式的理论结果。 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们详细介绍了第3节和附录B中的ATPO算法,以及第4.1节和附录C中的实验设置细节。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在附录C中提供了环境的细节,并将在出版时提供代码和脚本。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是]理由: 我们在第4.1节和附录C中描述了数据集、拆分、模型、评价指标、培训程序和关键超参数。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:理由: 我们注意到,进行多次培训将需要大大增加计算费用。 我们发现,各种模型和数据集的结果是一致的(第4.2、4.3和4.4节)。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们提供附录C.2中的资料。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 我们的研究是在严格遵守《新IPS守则》的情况下进行的。
道德观. • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 请见附录N。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文没有发布新的数据集或高风险模型. 对现有公共基准进行了实验。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们使用公开的数据集和模型,并引用其原始来源。 我们遵守他们的许可证和使用条件。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 该文件没有引入或释放新的资产。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文既不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文既不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[不详]理由: 在研究中,我们没有使用LLMs开发核心方法。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Please refer to the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 请参看摘要、导言和结论。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们详细介绍了第3节和附录B中的ATPO算法,以及第4.1节和附录C中的实验设置细节。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. blocks.en: Licenses for existing assets
blocks.zh: 现有资产的许可证

blocks.en: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守?

blocks.en: Justification: We use publicly available datasets and models and cite their original sources. We follow their respective licenses and terms of use.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
